c.tagline: A laid-back diving town on the Turquoise Coast, built over a half-submerged Lycian rock tomb

card: Widely accepted at hotels, restaurants, and dive shops; small local eateries may prefer cash.
rides: dolmuş minibuses to Kalkan and Patara

taxi.fare: Roughly ₺30-50 flag fall plus metered per-km rate
taxi.fareNote: Metered fares are standard; agree a flat rate for trips to Kalkan or Patara

walk: Central Kaş's harbor, market, and amphitheatre are all within a compact, walkable old town; Kaputaş Beach, Patara, and Kekova require a dolmuş, taxi, or boat.

safety.safety: Very safe for solo travelers, including women; Kaş has a relaxed, low-key atmosphere popular with independent and repeat travelers
safety.crime: Petty theft is rare; the town's small size and strong community feel keep crime very low

hood_landmark.Kaş Harbor / Old Town: Kaş amphitheatre and the harbor promenade
hood_landmark.Küçükçakıl / Büyükçakıl Beach: Kaş's small pebble beaches near town
hood_landmark.Çukurbağ Peninsula: Quiet boutique hotels along the peninsula road

hood_desc: The compact old town around the harbor, with the ancient amphitheatre, Friday market, and most restaurants and dive shops.
Kaş's small in-town pebble beaches, popular for an easy swim without leaving the center.
A quiet peninsula road lined with boutique hotels and sea-view guesthouses just outside the town center.

water.note: Most visitors and locals drink bottled water.

transit.sys: Dolmuş (shared minibus) network connecting Kaş to Kalkan and Patara
transit.map: Dolmuş depart from the Kaş otogar near the harbor
transit.note: Boat trips to Kekova's sunken city are a signature Kaş experience

transport.air: Dalaman Airport (DLM) or Antalya Airport (AYT), each about 2-2.5 hours away by road
transport.bus: Regional coaches connect Kaş to Antalya, Fethiye, and other Turquoise Coast towns
transport.ferry: Seasonal boat tours connect Kaş to nearby coastal sites; no scheduled international ferry
transport.car: Self-driving is popular for exploring Kaputaş, Patara, and Saklıkent independently

airport.name: Dalaman or Antalya Airport
airport.distance: ~2-2.5 hrs by road from either airport
airport.transport: Pre-booked shuttle or private transfer; taxi transfer roughly $90-130

net.w: Free wifi standard in hotels and cafes
net.fwn: Free wifi widely available in hotels and harbor cafes
net.ap: A Turkcell or Vodafone tourist SIM or eSIM is recommended

tip.s: 10% is customary for dive instructors and boat crews
tip.r: 10% is standard at restaurants where service isn't already included

food.name: Meze table
food.desc: A spread of cold Aegean-Mediterranean starters: samphire in olive oil, fava, hibes tahini-chilli dip, stuffed courgette flowers and octopus salad.

places.name: Nereid Meyhanesi
places.note: Upmarket seaside meyhane praised for rare mezes like lavinya and levrek simit alongside sea bass.

places.name: Uzum Kizi Meyhane
places.note: Terrace over the marina; classic meyhane meze trolley you pick from at the table.

places.name: Bahce Restaurant
places.area: Old Town, by the Lycian sarcophagus
places.note: Long-running garden restaurant known for its cold meze selection and shady courtyard.

food.name: Grilled fish
food.desc: Whole levrek (sea bass), cipura (sea bream) or lagos caught off the Lycian coast, salted and charcoal-grilled with rocket, lemon and olive oil.

places.name: Bahce Balik
places.note: The fish-focused sister of Bahce; whole catch of the day priced by weight.

places.name: Kurucesme Brasserie Balik ve Meze
places.note: Fish and meze house repeatedly listed among the town's best seafood spots.

places.name: Mercan Restaurant
places.note: Institution right on the harbour wall, serving grilled fish to boat crews for decades.

food.name: Gozleme
food.desc: Hand-rolled village flatbread cooked on a domed sac griddle and folded around white cheese and parsley, spinach, potato or minced meat.

places.name: Kas Weekly Market
places.note: Village women roll gozleme to order at the weekly producers' market; cheapest and most authentic in town.

places.name: Cukurbagi village tea gardens
places.note: Roadside tea gardens on the peninsula loop make gozleme fresh while you look over the bay.

places.name: Bi Lokma
places.note: Home-style kitchen popular for breakfast plates and griddle breads with a sea view.

food.name: Sikma
food.desc: Antalya-region wrap: a paper-thin yufka squeezed around grilled meat or cheese, tomato and herbs, then pressed on the griddle until crisp.

places.name: Kas Weekly Market
places.note: Griddle stalls make sikma alongside gozleme; the local breakfast-on-the-go.

places.name: Mupptela Ocakbasi
places.note: Grill house away from the tourist strip; generous portions and wraps off the charcoal.

places.name: Kas otogar snack stands
places.note: Workaday griddle counters where drivers and locals eat sikma through the morning.

food.name: Ocakbasi kebabs
food.desc: Charcoal-grilled lamb and chicken skewers, kofte and lamb chops served with flatbread, grilled peppers and Antalya piyazi tahini bean salad.

places.name: Mupptela Ocakbasi
places.note: Widely rated the most authentic grill in Kas and far cheaper than the harbour.

places.name: Kosk Restaurant
places.note: Stone-house restaurant mixing Anatolian grills with local mezes on a vine terrace.

places.name: Smiley's Restaurant
places.note: Long-established family grill and clay-pot testi kebab, a Kas fixture for years.

food.name: Kabak cicegi dolmasi
food.desc: Courgette flowers stuffed with herbed rice and gently poached in olive oil, a summer speciality of the western Mediterranean coast.

places.name: Bahce Restaurant
places.note: Seasonal olive-oil dishes are the house strength; flowers appear on the meze list in summer.

places.name: Nereid Meyhanesi
places.note: Kitchen leans on little-known local recipes, including stuffed flowers when in season.

places.name: Uzum Kizi Meyhane
places.note: Meze counter regularly carries olive-oil vegetable dishes made that morning.

food.name: Raki
food.desc: Aniseed spirit clouded with water and drunk slowly across a whole meze table with ice and melon or white cheese; the coast's ritual drink.

places.name: Nereid Meyhanesi
places.note: Proper meyhane service, with meze paced to match the raki rather than the other way round.

places.name: Uzum Kizi Meyhane
places.note: Sunset terrace over the marina, a favourite spot for the slow raki table.

places.name: Mercan Restaurant
places.note: Harbour-wall tables where locals settle in with raki and fish after the boats come in.

food.name: Nar suyu and Turkish tea
food.desc: Pomegranate and fresh orange juice pressed at street carts, plus tulip glasses of strong black tea poured all day in the shaded squares.

places.name: Cumhuriyet Meydani tea gardens
places.note: Shaded benches under the plane tree where the town drinks tea and plays backgammon.

places.name: Kas Weekly Market
places.note: Juice carts press pomegranate and orange to order beside the produce stalls.

places.name: Uzun Carsi juice stands
places.note: Row of pressers on the bougainvillea-covered shopping street, cheapest juice in the centre.

landmarks: Antiphellos Ancient Theatre
A beautifully preserved Hellenistic theatre gazing straight out to the Mediterranean, where sunset over the Greek islands steals the show from the stage.
Lion Tomb (King's Tomb)
A monumental 4th-century-BC Lycian sarcophagus standing improbably amid boutique shops on Uzun Çarşı street, crowned by carved lion-head handles.
Kaputaş Beach
A dazzling turquoise cove wedged between sheer canyon cliffs just up the coast, reached by 187 steps and endlessly featured on Turkey's postcards.
Kekova Sunken City
Boat tours glide over submerged Lycian ruins along Kekova island's shore, where earthquake-drowned staircases and walls shimmer beneath crystal-clear water.
Kaleköy (Simena) Castle
A roadless village crowned by a Byzantine castle containing the world's smallest Lycian theatre, overlooking sarcophagi that stand knee-deep in the sea.
Kaş Old Town and Harbour
Bougainvillea-draped whitewashed lanes spill down to a yacht-filled harbour, packing boutique charm, meyhanes and Lycian relics into Turkey's prettiest small resort.
Doric Rock Tomb
Carved entirely from bedrock above town in the 4th century BC, this austere Doric-style tomb offers antiquity with a panoramic bay view.
Limanağzı Bay
Accessible only by water taxi or coastal footpath, this sheltered swimming bay pairs beach platforms with Lycian rock tombs carved into its cliffs.
Büyük Çakıl Beach
The town's favourite pebble beach, a short stroll from the centre, where impossibly clear turquoise water invites long lazy swimming days.
Kastellorizo (Meis) Island
A twenty-minute ferry crosses to this colourful Greek harbour island, famed for its neoclassical waterfront and the luminous Blue Grotto sea cave.

train.note: There is no railway on the Lycian coast, so no trains reach Kaş. The nearest station is at Denizli, some 5 hours inland. Arrive by coach along the coast road or fly into Antalya or Dalaman and continue by bus.

bus.note: No international coaches. Kaş's small otogar has services along the coast to Antalya (about 3h30 via Demre and Finike), Fethiye (2 hours) and onward connections to Istanbul, on Batı Antalya and Kamil Koç (https://www.kamilkoc.com.tr/). Book through obilet (https://www.obilet.com/en/). Dolmuş minibuses run to Kalkan and Patara.

intl.to: Kastellorizo / Meis (Greece) - ~20 min from Kaş harbour

ferry.note: Kaş has the shortest international crossing in Turkey: the boat to the tiny Greek island of Kastellorizo (Meis) takes about 20 minutes from the town harbour and runs daily in summer, dropping to a few sailings a week in winter. Bring your passport - it is a full border crossing despite the distance - and note that Kastellorizo has onward ferry links to Rhodes only a couple of times a week.

half.name: Patara
half.blurb: A 20-kilometer sand beach fronts the ruins of a Lycian league capital, including a triple-arched gate and a silted-in harbor.

half.name: Xanthos
half.blurb: Pillar tombs and a Roman theater remain from the former capital of ancient Lycia, a UNESCO World Heritage site.

half.name: Saklıkent Gorge
half.blurb: A 300-meter-deep canyon carved by meltwater runs for about 18 kilometers through the Akdağ mountains.

half.name: Demre
half.blurb: The Byzantine-era Church of St. Nicholas and the rock-cut tombs of ancient Myra sit in this town once known as the bishop's home.
